newsitem.title: USA: MCI keeps local plans as review continues.
newsitem.headline: MCI keeps local plans as review continues.

text.p: MCI Communications Corp's joint review of operations with merger partner British Telecommunications Plc will take several more weeks, MCI's chief financial officer said Wednesday.

But CFO Doug Maine said his company remained committed to making hefty investments to enter U.S. local phone markets, despite the expected impact on MCI earnings for the remainder of 1997 and throughout 1998.
"MCI will be among the first long distance carriers to offer local service nationally," Maine said.
"MCI is never slow to seize opportunity. Now is exactly the time to make our move into local," he said.
"We expect that this (review) will take weeks rather than months," Maine said of BT and MCI's joint operations review.
He made the remarks in a conference call with analysts and reporters following the release of MCI's second quarter results.

MCI's move into U.S. local phone markets has led to calls from BT shareholders for a reevaluation of the terms of the proposed BT-MCI merger in light of increased dilution to earnings that are seen resulting from local entry delays.

The U.S. long distance provider has said its local service bid is being impeded by foot-dragging among Baby Bell operators in opening local markets to competition and by the glacial pace of U.S. local phone deregulation efforts.

MCI has begun offering local phone service in 25 metropolitan regions to date. It began service in New Jersey only last week. It has said it plans to offer service in at least 31 U.S. local markets by year-end.
Published reports have said the jobs of Maine and MCI President Timothy Price could be on the line following MCI's surprise warning on July 10 about lower results ahead.
During the conference call, Maine reiterated that further review of local service strategies could lead to material charges to 1997 results.
He said second quarter capital spending totaled $970 million, up from $750 million in the first quarter and $900 million in the 1996 second quarter.

He said MCI had the lowest revenue-to-call-traffic gap of any major U.S. long distance carrier and that consolidated company revenues grew faster during the second quarter than those of rivals AT&T Corp and Sprint Corp.

MCI long distance revenues grew 4.7 percent to $4.4 billion, while overall revenues, including new ventures and developing markets, grew 6 percent to $4.8 billion. Long distance traffic volumes grew 5.5 percent.

By contrast, overall AT&T revenues grew 1.5 percent while Sprint total revenues grew 5.8 percent, although Sprint's long distance business grew at 8.1 percent, nearly twice as fast as MCI's during the second quarter.
Maine said second quarter operating expenses rose 2.9 percent, or less than half the pace of overall revenue growth.
MCI shares fell in early trading Wednesday following the release of its second quarter results. The stock was down 1/2 to 35-1/4 at 1046 EDT/1446 GMT.
BT shares stood at 430 pence, up 6-1/2 pence, or approximately where they traded ahead of the release of MCI's results.
